page: Amazon Web Services m6i.32xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 128 vCPUs (64 physical cores with hyperthreading) utilizing Intel Xeon 8375C processors running at 3.5 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by a 54 MB L3 cache and advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and cryptographic acceleration. Memory capacity stands at 512.0 GB of DDR4 RAM operating at 3 GHz, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is not bundled with this instance type, requiring external network-attached storage, while network connectivity delivers a baseline bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the m6i.32xlarge demonstrates strong multi-core performance. The Passmark CPU score and CPU encryption tests rank in the top tier, reflecting high computational density for parallel workloads. Memory bandwidth is also highly efficient, with large-block read operations reaching 333.99 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25 percent of tested systems. However, single-core performance metrics, such as stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores, fall into the average category. For machine learning workloads, the instance handles prompt processing for medium-sized 7B models efficiently, but text generation for large 70B models is weak, representing a performance tradeoff for heavy AI inference without dedicated GPU acceleration.

This server offers high resource density, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for enterprise-scale workloads that require substantial memory and compute resources without the premium cost of specialized GPU or high-speed local NVMe hardware. It is highly suited for multi-threaded applications, database operations, static web serving, and software compilation.
description: Amazon Web Services m6i.32xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 128 vCPUs and 512.0 GB of DDR4 RAM, powered by Intel Xeon 8375C processors at 3.5 GHz. Operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, this x86_64 server delivers a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It lacks local storage and GPU accelerators but provides a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps. Benchmarks indicate top-tier multi-core CPU and encryption performance, alongside strong memory bandwidth and database operations. However, single-core performance and large-scale LLM text generation remain average to weak. This instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for resource-dense, parallelized workloads, making it highly suitable for enterprise databases, multi-threaded software compilation, static web serving, and medium-scale containerized deployments.
